_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED/authored files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282. aws-billing 4.34.2 reprint: the fleet replay pinned the generic base_url probe, which on this synthetic connector would call a healthy install's nominal base_url a placeholder; the asserts pin the AWS doctor instead (awsDoctorReport owns api and credentials). Kit adoption (credkit-wiring): the cliutil.ShowOwnValue marker left with the connector's output chokepoint; the kit shows the doctor's own verdicts unchanged (TestDoctorJSONShowsItsOwnVerdicts).

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: sts:GetCallerIdentity failed (no AWS credential resolved, or AWS refused it)"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For aws-billing the manifest gained: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_BILLING_BASE_URL, AWS_BILLING_SLACK_CHANNEL, AWS_REGION, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN. server.json gained: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_BILLING_BASE_URL, AWS_BILLING_SLACK_CHANNEL, AWS_REGION, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_BILLING_BASE_URL, AWS_BILLING_SLACK_CHANNEL, AWS_REGION, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: report --post-slack delegates to slack-pp-cli; the channel (MCP-settable via --slack-channel) and summary are joined to their flags as one argv element each (--channel=<v>, --text=<v>) via slackMessageArgs.
handfixes.why: Codex round-two review of the fleet mcp-argv-value-joined backport (2026-09-09): this is the only downstream argv reconstruction in the fleet that re-emits an MCP-settable value as a separate element (--channel <v>). It is safe only while slack-pp-cli keeps --channel a value-consuming string flag - a parser outside this repository. Joined, a value beginning with '--' stays contained inside its own element regardless of the child's flag types. report.go is novel code, so a reprint does not touch it, but the ledger keeps the intent visible and the assert keeps the split form from returning.

handfixes.summary: cmd/aws-billing-mcp/main.go declares `var version = "0.0.0-dev"` and passes it to server.NewMCPServer, so release.yml's `-X main.version=<tag>` stamps the real release into serverInfo.version (issue #322, PR #323)
handfixes.why: Issue #322: the MCP binary reported a hard-coded literal ("1.0.0") in serverInfo.version instead of the release tag. release.yml builds every MCP with `-ldflags "-X main.version=${version}"` (PR #323) and the press template emits `var version = "0.0.0-dev"` for 63 of 67 connectors; this connector's main.go had drifted to a literal in the NewMCPServer call, and the Go linker silently ignores a -X for a symbol that does not exist (build exit 0, no warning), so the stamp could never land. Proven both ways with a real initialize JSON-RPC over stdio: before the fix `go build -ldflags '-X main.version=9.9.9'` still answered the literal; after it answers 9.9.9. A wrong-looking real version (1.0.0 on a v0.1.x release) is worse than 0.0.0-dev because it reads as intentional. code_only because the explanatory comment above the var names the ldflags mechanism; the assert must be satisfied by the declaration itself.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: None needed at the press: current cli-printing-press already emits the var and passes it (see any of the 63 standard mains). A reprint from any current press regenerates this correctly; retire the entry after the next reprint confirms the var is present.

handfixes.summary: sync and workflow archive run the AWS sync with an outcome per layer (accounts, costs, forecasts, inventory: a layer fails when its AWS call failed or any row could not be stored); resources_synced is the count of layers that synced, and both commands exit non-zero when every attempted layer failed
handfixes.why: Issue #275 finding 3 on this connector, fixed in the 4.34.2 reprint (the tripwire this entry was is replaced by the fix's markers): runAWSSync folded every AWS failure into a warning and dropped store errors, and the archive hard-coded resources_synced 4, so an all-denied or all-failed sync or archive exited 0 and read as an empty account. Partial success stays exit 0 with warnings. Seen failing: seen/sync-all-failed-json, sync-all-failed-human, archive-all-failed.

handfixes.summary: SiblingCLIPath tries the sibling `aws-billing-cli.exe` then the bare `aws-billing-cli` on Windows and looks up `aws-billing-cli.exe` on PATH there, matching the hudu-era press shape (siblingCLICandidates / cliExecutableName)
handfixes.why: Found by Codex reviewing the companion-CLI bundle (2026-09-18, census with riverside-fm and rewst): the 4.19.0 print's cli_path.go stat'ed exactly one sibling name - cliExecutableName(runtime.GOOS), i.e. only `aws-billing-cli.exe` on Windows and only the bare name elsewhere - with no fallback to the other spelling, and no ordered candidate list. A Windows bundle or install that carries the CLI under either spelling must resolve it before falling through to AWS_BILLING_CLI_PATH and PATH, or every Cobra-mirror MCP tool fails with a missing companion. Ported hudu's shape verbatim with the slug swapped: sibling .exe first on windows, then bare; then AWS_BILLING_CLI_PATH; then exec.LookPath of the per-OS executable name. cli_path_test.go pins the candidate order per GOOS without needing a Windows runner. GENERATOR-class: a reprint from a press older than the one that introduced siblingCLICandidates restores the single-candidate lookup; retire after a reprint from a current press confirms the shape is regenerated. DONE UPSTREAM: mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#4787 merged 2026-09-23 (closed #4745), first shipped press v4.32.5; this hand-fix stays active until a reprint absorbs it; do NOT cite #4745 as open. Upstream receipt: internal/generator/templates/cobratree/cli_path.go.tmpl:17 SiblingCLIPath now passes runtime.GOOS AND runtime.GOARCH; siblingCLICandidates(goos, goarch, exePath string) at :32-48 tries the bare name, <bare>-<GOOS>-<GOARCH>, then <bare>-<GOOS>, each as .exe first on windows and then extensionless; the <PREFIX>_CLI_PATH override and exec.LookPath(cliExecutableName(runtime.GOOS)) at :26 are unchanged. The hudu-era two-argument signature this entry asserts is NOT what a 4.32.5 print emits: The asserts here pin THIS connector's hand-fix shape, not the 4.32.5 template shape, so at the absorbing reprint re-pin them to the regenerated shape rather than reading the gate failure as a regression. Re-pinned at the 4.34.2 reprint to the regenerated three-argument shape.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: None: the press already emits this shape (hudu and the other 4.24+ prints carry it). Regenerated by the next reprint.

handfixes.summary: The on-disk response cache is off on every client: raw AWS bodies never sit in cache files.
handfixes.why: Work order: nothing but the credential store holds a credential, and a cached answer to another request is a wrong-data class (Codex cache-answer-not-the-request). c.NoCache = true in the client hook (internal/cli/awsbilling_guard.go); TestClientHookTurnsTheCacheOffAndDryRunSendsNothing asserts it. Kit adoption: the kit makes a cache write safe from a held value (credkit.WriteFile), not a cached answer right, so the cache stays off. README and SKILL say responses are never cached.

handfixes.why: Defense in depth beside dry-run-never-mints: the generated preview path returns before sending, and this transport makes a missed branch fail closed. The black-box test runs writes and auth login under --dry-run from a cold start against a fake token host and API host and counts zero requests on both. handfixes.summary: export --output closes its (kit) output file on every return, including an API error: the open no longer shadows RunE's named err
handfixes.why: The generated `f, err := openExportOutput(...)` inside the --output block declared a new err, so the deferred close tested that inner (nil) err and never ran when the export returned an API error. With the output chokepoint the file is a filter pipe, and the unclosed pipe kept the process from exiting: `export clients --output f.jsonl` after a 401 hung (TestExportOutputReturnsAfterAnAPIError, seen failing 3 of 4 runs). Fleet note: every connector that took the ported chokepoint edit on export.go carries the same shadowing. Ported to aws-billing from the gradient 4.34.2 reprint (one credential layer across the fleet). Ported to aws-billing from the liongard 4.34.2 reprint (one credential layer across the fleet). Ported to aws-billing from the abnormal 4.34.2 reprint (one credential layer across the fleet). Kit adoption (credkit-wiring): openExportOutput returns a credkit.Writer over credkit.OpenFile; the shadowing fix is unchanged.

handfixes.summary: Every AWS SDK request (service calls and the SDK's credential providers) goes only to an AWS endpoint of a service this connector calls (ce, organizations, sts, ec2, monitoring, s3, portal.sso, oidc, signin) over https:443, or to the ECS and EKS Pod Identity container-credential addresses over http (EC2 instance metadata is off: r1b-imds-off); a custom endpoint (AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, endpoint_url) and every redirect hop are refused. The pin runs in the transport's per-request proxy hook, inside credkit.Transport, so proxies keep working; a custom CA bundle (AWS_CA_BUNDLE, ca_bundle) is refused with a clear error; S3 is path-style
handfixes.why: Credential rule host pinning on the AWS path: the SDK signs with the operator's keys and sends the session token in X-Amz-Security-Token to whatever endpoint it resolves, and it honours AWS_ENDPOINT_URL and endpoint_url. The published tree had no pin. A custom http.Client would break AWS_CA_BUNDLE (the SDK requires its BuildableClient), so the check sits in http.Transport.Proxy, which every request and redirect hop passes before it dials. Seen failing: seen/aws-endpoint-pin-seen-failing.log (TestCustomEndpointNeverReceivesASignedRequest). Kit adoption (credkit-wiring): the SDK gets &http.Client{Transport: credkit.Transport(pinned transport)} for every client and credential provider. The SDK applies a CA bundle only to its own BuildableClient, so with the kit's client a custom bundle is refused up front instead of ignored.

handfixes.summary: A request the AWS guard refuses (another host, a redirect hop, a --dry-run send) is not retryable, so the SDK fails at once instead of retrying with backoff
handfixes.why: Black-box suite class refusal-retried: the SDK read a refusal as a connection error and retried it (three attempts per operation and per credential refresh), so a sync against a refused endpoint took 73 seconds to fail. Seen failing: seen/bb-refusal-retried-seen-failing.log.

handfixes.summary: The AWS transport speaks HTTP/1.1 only (empty TLSNextProto, ALPN http/1.1), so every request, including one on a reused connection, passes the proxy hook where the pin, the redirect refusal, and the dry-run refusal run
handfixes.why: Black-box suite class pin-skipped-on-reused-connection: on a cached HTTP/2 connection the SDK's transport skips the proxy hook, so a same-origin redirect hop was followed. Seen failing: seen/bb-pin-skipped-on-reused-connection-seen-failing.log.

handfixes.summary: The black-box suite reaches its fake AWS only in a build with the awsbilling_blackbox tag: that build dials the fake for every https connection to port 443 and trusts the fake's certificate, while every request keeps its real AWS host, so the pin and the kit's origins apply unchanged; a release binary has neither the hook value nor the environment variables
handfixes.why: The suite must run the real binaries against a fake AWS without adding a runtime override to a release build. Seen failing: seen/bb-test-endpoint-in-production-seen-failing.log. Kit adoption (credkit-wiring): the hook moved from admitting a loopback origin to redirecting the dial, so the suite exercises the production origin rules (credkit.Transport and awsEndpointAllowed) instead of a test-only exception to them.

handfixes.summary: The container credential provider (ECS, EKS Pod Identity, AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_FULL_URI) uses the pinned HTTP client, like every other SDK client: its authorization token and the credentials it fetches go only to the pinned AWS and credential-service addresses
handfixes.why: Codex r1 class credential-sent-to-another-host: config's resolveHTTPCredProvider builds endpointcreds without the configured HTTPClient, so it fell back to a client of its own and skipped the pin; with AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_FULL_URI=https://collector.example/credentials the token went there. A held value in the report --out path is no longer refused: the kit does not check file names (a P2 follow-up).

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand and replaces this connector's own credential layer. internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one Declarations literal: the AWS credential variables and their aliases, the container authorization token and the MCP HTTP bearer (sent nowhere); the shared credentials file, the SSO and login token caches, the web identity and container token files and the press config as Files; the AWS config file's credential keys held by holdAWSConfig (the kit would hold every value of that file); SigV4's X-Amz-Security-Token and the SSO bearer as headers; the STS, SSO and container answers as response fields; AWS endpoints and the generated client's base_url as origins. Each main starts with credkit.Start and ends with credkit.Exit; the AWS SDK (every client and credential provider) and the generated, feedback, deliver and probe clients go through credkit.Transport; every credential the SDK retrieves is held (HoldMinted); every file write, the MCP stdio and HTTP servers, MCP tool calls and every child process go through the kit.
handfixes.why: Retires secret-echo-decoded-funnel, journal-credential-hardening, output-chokepoint, file-sinks-withheld, store-never-keeps-secrets, mcp-protocol-messages-withheld, network-sinks-withheld, startup-output-held-first, mcp-held-arguments-refused, undecoded-encodings-every-alignment, held-forms-in-every-encoding, response-credentials-held, every-text-encoding-withheld, outbound-split-parts-refused, auth-carrier-names-and-shapes-held, secure-container-is-credential, r1-holder-reads-every-part, r1-mixed-byte-escapes-decoded, r1-split-across-deliveries-withheld, api-origin-pinned, held-value-case-folded, output-units-reassembled, preclose-holder-numbers-and-cookies, preclose-escape-fixpoint, preclose-split-across-processes-and-protocol, refuse-held-uses-connector-chokepoint, output-derived-and-scheme-forms-matched-whole, g304-paths-cleaned-not-annotated, r1-short-value-encodings-withheld, r1-file-history-is-the-whole-file, r2-short-value-nested-encodings, aws-credentials-held, config-file-holds-no-credential, bb-store-split-halves, bb-value-cut-before-chokepoint, bb-split-across-tool-results, bb-own-output-shown, r1-holder-reads-every-sdk-source, r2-holder-reads-as-the-sdk: replaced by the shared credential kit (entries removed: the ledger's retired list only takes retirements tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json backs). That layer (the awsbilling_* holder, output chokepoint and encoding detectors, the secret funnel, the SDK-ini credential reader, the journal credential checks, the store's withholding driver, the own-value marker) grew per review round because each sink and encoding was closed one at a time. The kit is one shared implementation of docs/credential-leak-contract.md, checked byte for byte against tools/maintainer/credkit (vendor_credkit.py --check). The black-box suite (internal/awsbillingblackbox) drives the built CLI and MCP binaries against a fake AWS that echoes held values: every source signs and every sink writes, no sink carries an echoed credential, startup output never shows a malformed file's credential, and the Codex r2 inputs (credential-handed-to-another-program, holder-incomplete, cache-answer-not-the-request) were each seen failing on the pre-kit tree or with the kit sink unrouted. Known limits, documented: a custom CA bundle is refused, a container credential endpoint that needs an authorization token over plain http is refused by the kit, and the kit does not check output file names.

handfixes.summary: The AWS SDK's EC2 instance-metadata client is off in every config the connector loads (awsx loadConfig, the one LoadDefaultConfig call, used by every CLI command and so by every MCP tool, which runs the CLI): config.WithEC2IMDSClientEnableState(imds.ClientDisabled) is the config's first source, so it wins over AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED and the shared config, and every IMDS client the SDK builds from the config (the instance-role credential provider, defaults_mode auto) sends nothing. The endpoint pin no longer allows 169.254.169.254 or fd00:ec2::254 over plain http. A credential chain that ends at instance metadata fails with a fixed error saying instance-metadata credentials are not used. The container credential addresses stay as they were: a request there carrying an authorization token is refused by the kit (the token is held; no held value goes over plain http).
handfixes.why: Codex r1 (finding at internal/credwire/declarations.go:72), RELEASE RULE item 2: on EC2 with no other credential source, the SDK's IMDS client minted an IMDSv2 token and sent it in x-aws-ec2-metadata-token to http://169.254.169.254, and read the instance role's credentials back, over plain http; the pin explicitly allowed the address. Confirmed on the production binary (HTTP proxy pointed at a fake instance-metadata service): the token was sent twice over plain http. Seen failing: seen/r1fix-credential-sent-over-plain-http-seen-failing.log; passing: seen/r1fix-credential-sent-over-plain-http-seen-passing.log; fix reverted: seen/r1fix-credential-sent-over-plain-http-seen-reverted.log.

handfixes.summary: Every credential that signs an outgoing AWS request is held before the request is sent, whatever provider produced it and at any depth of an assume-role chain: the pinned transport's per-request hook (pinTransport, which the kit's guard runs on every request before it judges it and outside its locks) calls holdSigners, which holds the access key ID of every SigV4 Authorization header and presigned X-Amz-Credential, and every X-Amz-Security-Token header or query value (names in any case), with HoldMinted. Fail closed: an https request (every one the pin allows goes to an AWS endpoint) whose Authorization is not a SigV4 signature the parser reads is refused (non-retryable). holdingProvider still holds the final credentials' secret key.
handfixes.why: Codex r1 (finding at internal/awsx/awsbilling_guard.go:244): holdingProvider wraps only the outermost provider, and the SDK signs the STS AssumeRole call of an assume-role chain with the source profile's credentials, which it never returns; SigV4 Authorization is an exempt identifier source, so the source access key ID was never held. Confirmed on the built binary: a credential_process source_profile whose STS AssumeRole answered AccessDenied quoting the signing key printed the key on stderr and in the MCP result. Static keys in the shared credentials file did not reproduce (held from startup); the class fix covers every source. One fake-AWS run of the successful chain through the kit-wired binary shows the hold inside the round trip does not deadlock. Seen failing: seen/r1fix-credential-used-but-not-held-seen-failing.log; passing: seen/r1fix-credential-used-but-not-held-seen-passing.log; fix reverted: seen/r1fix-credential-used-but-not-held-seen-reverted.log.

handfixes.summary: Every stored inventory read (ensureInventory: every waste subcommand, report and ask, CLI and MCP, which runs the CLI) answers for exactly the one region a live read scans, resolved the same way: awsReadOpts.inventoryRegion is the command's client region, or awsx.ResolveRegion, which loads the config through the same loadConfig as awsx.New (--region, AWS_REGION, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, the profile's region, else us-east-1) and needs no request, so --data-source local resolves it too; a region that cannot be resolved is an error naming --region. store.InventoryIfScanned refuses a read naming no region and reads only that region's scan (and the account-wide S3 bucket rows). Cost Explorer, forecast and Organizations reads are global and not keyed by region.
handfixes.why: Codex r1 (finding at internal/cli/awsdata.go:190), class cache-answer-not-the-request: a stored read with no --region passed an empty region, which accepted every scanned region, while the live path scans the SDK-resolved region; so `sync --skip-cost --region us-east-1` followed by `AWS_REGION=us-west-2 waste rank --json` answered with us-east-1 waste. Confirmed on the built binary for AWS_REGION, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION and the profile's region, auto and --data-source local, and the MCP waste_rank tool. Seen failing: seen/r1fix-cache-answer-not-the-request-region-seen-failing.log; passing: seen/r1fix-cache-answer-not-the-request-region-seen-passing.log; fix reverted: seen/r1fix-cache-answer-not-the-request-region-seen-reverted.log.

handfixes.summary: holdAWSConfig (internal/credwire/declarations.go) names the credential kit one path per web_identity_token_file in ~/.aws/config: the value as the SDK reads it (config/internal/ini: cut at the first ' #', ' ;', tab-# or tab-;, then trimmed; sdkPropertyValue). It no longer names the untrimmed or otherwise cut variants, which the SDK never opens.
handfixes.why: Windows CI on PR #607: TestR1HolderReadsEverySDKCredentialSource saw recall print nothing. The untrimmed value is ' C:\\...' on Windows, no file name at all; the kit cannot stat it, cannot tell it from an unreadable credential file, marks the held set unknown and withholds every write of the run, its notices included (exit 74, no output). Reproduced on macOS with a regular file named ' ' in the working directory (TestR1cConfigTokenFileNamedAsTheSDKOpensIt, seen failing before the fix). The token file's contents stay held: the path named is the one the SDK opens.
